test_path: (no dedicated test — module is a trivial singleton; consumed by every inngest/functions/__tests__/*.test.ts)
uncertainty_notes: Module is a 21-line Inngest singleton: `new Inngest({ id: 'roas-dashboard' })`. INNGEST_EVENT_KEY is read automatically from process.env by the SDK when not passed explicitly (Vercel Marketplace integration injects it per the inline comment). The id 'roas-dashboard' matches Inngest's lowercase-with-dash convention and is used as the routing key in Inngest Cloud UI. No mutable state, no environment-dependent branching, no externally observable behavior beyond Inngest.send(...) calls in downstream functions. Indirect coverage is comprehensive: every inngest/functions/__tests__/*.test.ts imports a module that imports `inngest` from here. If the singleton were misconfigured (e.g. wrong id, throwing constructor), all of cronDaily/cronLive/cronWhatsapp/events test suites would fail at module import time. No bug found.

test_coverage_gaps.description: No explicit test pinning `inngest.id === 'roas-dashboard'`. A typo (e.g. 'road-dashboard') would still let all sibling tests pass because they mock the SDK or call inner handlers directly; only the production webhook route at /api/inngest would silently route to the wrong Inngest Cloud app.
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: Inngest's serve() endpoint uses the client's id as the routing key. A drift between this id and what's configured in the Inngest Cloud dashboard would cause production cron triggers to silently route nowhere — operator would see green Inngest dev console but zero firings.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Add tiny test: `import { inngest } from '@/inngest/client'; expect(inngest.id).toBe('roas-dashboard');` — single assertion guards against typo refactors.

test_coverage_gaps.description: No test for the absence/presence of eventKey wiring. If a future refactor passes `eventKey: undefined` explicitly (rather than omitting), the SDK behavior changes (Inngest treats explicit undefined as 'no key', not 'read from env').
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: Subtle — but inngest.send() in production would fail authentication silently if eventKey wiring regressed.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Snapshot test on `(inngest as any).options` shape, or assert that no `eventKey` key appears in the constructor args literal (AST-style).
